standard_prerequisites.name: Derived completion of an object is the derived limit of its derived tensor products with the Koszul complexes on the powers of a generating set
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the completion into a derived limit so that its cohomology can be computed from the Koszul system.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a system of complexes there is a short exact sequence expressing the cohomology of the derived limit through the first derived limit and the limit of the cohomologies
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the displayed short exact sequence from which the vanishing of the cohomology of the completion is read off.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Koszul complex on the n-th powers of r generators sits in degrees from -r to 0, so tensor products with it vanish in the corresponding range of degrees
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the degree ranges in which the cone of the given morphism has vanishing cohomology after tensoring with the Koszul system, which pins down the vanishing range for the completion.

core_obligations: Write the ideal as generated by r elements, use the Koszul description of derived completion to write the completion of an object as the derived limit of its derived tensor products with the Koszul complexes, and record the resulting short exact sequence expressing the cohomology of the completion through the first derived limit and the limit of cohomologies (proof lines 26524-26532).

For part (1), take the cone of the given morphism: its cohomology vanishes in degrees at least zero, and since the Koszul complex sits in degrees at most zero, the tensor products of the cone with the Koszul complexes have vanishing cohomology in degrees at least zero, while the degree minus one term is a system with surjective transition maps (proof lines 26534-26541).

Conclude from the displayed sequence that the cohomology of the completion of the cone vanishes in degrees at least zero, and apply the distinguished triangle relating the completions of the three objects to obtain part (1) (proof lines 26541-26543).

For part (2), take the cone of the given morphism: its cohomology vanishes in degrees below zero, and since the Koszul complex sits in degrees from -r to 0 the tensor products with it vanish below degree -r; the displayed sequence then gives vanishing of the cohomology of the completion of the cone below degree r, which yields part (2) by the same triangle argument (proof lines 26545-26552).
proof_roadmap: Express derived completion through the Koszul system and record the short exact sequence for its cohomology (proof lines 26524-26532).
For (1), show the cone has vanishing tensor cohomology in nonnegative degrees and conclude (proof lines 26534-26543).
For (2), use the degree range -r to 0 of the Koszul complex to get vanishing below the shifted range and conclude (proof lines 26545-26552).
difficulty_reason: The statement is that derived completion with respect to an ideal generated by r elements has finite cohomological dimension, in the form of two statements comparing the completions along a morphism whose cohomology is an isomorphism in a range: one for the range at least one, and one for the range at most minus one with a shift of r (statement lines 26507-26522). The proof writes the completion as a derived limit of Koszul complexes, obtains the short exact sequence computing its cohomology, and then analyses the cone of the given morphism in the two cases: in the first case the cone vanishes in nonnegative degrees and the Koszul complexes sit in nonpositive degrees, while in the second the Koszul complexes sit between minus r and zero, which produces the shift visible in the statement (proof lines 26524-26552). The degree bookkeeping around the displayed sequence is what makes both assertions follow from the same computation.
